C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM.Name: One notification system: a single token-based card (icon-chip, four severities) replaces the legacy Fluent toast service and the bespoke C-66 update notice, adds copy-on-select with a quiet double-pulse confirmation, typed action buttons, a severity x source event model with dedup, and a session notification history opened from the command palette
C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM.ApprovalBasis: Owner approved the full design interactively on 2026-10-23 (icon-chip variant, double-pulse copy confirmation, palette-first history, severity x source model, toast/banner/modal boundary) and issued the execution instruction "делай" over the draft spec, authorizing plan and implementation under the standing four-corner review protocol (Correctness/Security/UX/Perf, CornerMatrix, repeated to two consecutive clean passes before handoff).
C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM.Summary: Mark today renders transient messages through four unrelated surfaces: the legacy MarkText Fluent toast (services/notification — blur-circle effect, JS geometry, Windows-era styling), the C-66 update notice (a card on theme tokens that the owner calls the only good-looking one), the per-file editor banner, and the zoom pill. The legacy service also carries dialog semantics it should never have had (showConfirm resolves/rejects a Promise inside a 10-second toast), and one of its store actions (SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING) is dead code with an orphan locale key. This change replaces the toast service's rendering layer with one card renderer in the C-66 visual family — severity icon in a 14% tinted circular chip (owner decision 2026-10-23: "icon-chip is cleaner, we take it"), radius/padding/shadow/button metrics inherited from the update notice, icons from the chromeIcons 16-grid set — and moves the update notice itself onto the same renderer with zero store-semantics change. Around that card the change builds the system agreed with the owner on 2026-10-23: a single bottom-right stack (max 3 visible, "More N notifications" overflow chip with per-locale plurals), severity x source event model (file / export / project / update / agent / system) with dedupKey collapsing and sticky errors, typed actions[] (copy / retry / open / reveal built-ins plus custom label+handler; primary / normal / quiet styles) governed by a no-answer-owed contract, copy-on-select for card text confirmed only by a double green pulse of the selection itself (a quiet developer feature, no label, invisible to users who never select), and a session-scoped notification history (cap 50, FIFO) opened by a command-palette entry. The per-file banner stays a banner — it is the sanctioned home for contextual questions with a safe default (file-changed-on-disk) — and is reskinned to the same tokens with selectable text. Dead SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING code, its unit test and the orphan installPandoc locale key are removed. Roughly 70 notify() call sites keep their call shape; the service API only gains optional fields.

Problem.Description: Four divergent notification surfaces ship in one app: services/notification/index.js renders .mt-notification Fluent toasts (mousemove blur circle, repositioning math in JS, colors from a separate --notification* token family), components/updateNotice renders a theme-token card the owner explicitly likes, components/editorWithTabs/notifications.vue renders a per-file banner with user-select: none, and the zoom pill is its own module. Consequences: (1) visual inconsistency — the owner, 2026-10-23 (translated from Russian): "the cute balloon in the corner only appears for updates, the other balloons are scary-looking — bring everything to a proper design system"; (2) positional conflict — the legacy toast (right/bottom 15px, z-index 10000) and the update notice (right/bottom 20px, z-index 900) occupy the same corner and overlap when both appear; (3) anti-pattern semantics — notify({showConfirm}) turns a self-dismissing toast into a yes/no dialog: clicking a check circle resolves a Promise, the X rejects it, timeout leaves it pending forever; two live call sites (store/editor.js image-deletion URL copy, showItemInFolder reveal) are shortcut actions mis-modeled as confirmations; (4) dead code — SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING has no production caller since audit-M-1 removed its IPC routes, yet ships with a unit test and an installPandoc locale key with no consumer; (5) no notification is recoverable — a toast that vanishes after 10 seconds takes its text with it, and error text (paths, reasons) is exactly what a developer wants to copy. The owner requested on 2026-10-23: unify to a design system, make text copyable via select-then-release ("a developer feature; nobody selects that text unless they need it"), and think about what else the system needs — which produced the history, dedup, actions and boundary decisions recorded in design-context.xml.

Goals.R-1: One card renderer, four severities: info, success, warning, error. Visual language is the icon-chip variant from the approved 2026-10-23 mock: severity glyph (chromeIcons 16-grid, 1.4 stroke) inside a circular chip tinted at 14% of the severity color, on the C-66 card metrics (radius 12, padding ~14-16, floatBg surface, floatShadow + floatBorder ring, max-width 320). Severity colors are new per-theme tokens supplied by every theme; Paper/Ink values from the mock (Paper info #3D6AD6 / success #2F9E63 / warning #C46510 / error #D5453C; Ink #82A9F7 / #6BCB90 / #F5A83C / #F87A72). Theme-token-only styling per the AGENTS design rule; no color literals in components.
Goals.R-2: One bottom-right stack shared by all corner notices: legacy toasts and the update notice queue in a single ordered stack (10px gaps) instead of overlapping siblings. Max 3 visible cards; older ones collapse into an "More N notifications" overflow chip with correct plural forms per locale. Behavior: hover pauses auto-dismiss timers; Esc dismisses the topmost card; error cards are sticky (no timer, no timer hairline); success/info/warning auto-dismiss with a thin severity-colored timer hairline along the card bottom; clicking a card with an active text selection never dismisses it (selection release must not double as a close click); prefers-reduced-motion drops all animation, timers still run.
Goals.R-3: Copy-on-select: text inside notification cards is selectable (user-select: text). Releasing the mouse with a non-empty selection contained in a card writes exactly the selection to the clipboard. The only confirmation is the selection itself double-pulsing in the success color (two ~250 ms pulses inside ~1.1 s, then the resting selection tint returns; animation class removed on animationend); no label, no bubble, no extra element anywhere (owner decision 2026-10-23, replacing two rejected designs — corner pill and selection bubble — recorded in design-context.xml). Under prefers-reduced-motion the copy is silent. This is a deliberately quiet developer feature: nothing is visible to users who never select notification text.
Goals.R-4: Typed actions[] replaces showConfirm: notify() accepts optional actions — built-in kinds copy / retry / open / reveal with payload, plus custom label+handler entries. Buttons render in the three C-66 styles: primary (accent fill), normal (inputBg), quiet (underlined, editorColor50). Contract (normative, enforced by review and tests): every action is safe to ignore (unanswered implies a safe default already holds), safe to repeat (idempotent from the user's viewpoint), and owed no answer (fire-and-forget; the API returns nothing promise-like). The two live showConfirm call sites migrate to actions[]: image-deletion URL becomes a copy action; showItemInFolder becomes a reveal action. The showConfirm flag and its Promise semantics are removed from the service API. Questions that need an answer never enter the toast system — they belong to the banner (contextual, safe default) or a modal (no safe default / data risk), per the boundary test in design-context.xml.
Goals.R-5: Severity x source event model: notify({ severity, source, title, message, actions, dedupKey, sticky, time }). severity drives appearance (R-1); source is a small enum — file, export, project, update, agent, system — rendered as a subtle label on the card and stored on history entries. Optional dedupKey: while a card with the same key is live (or within a short window), repeats do not spawn new cards but bump a visible xN counter on the existing one (the macOS notification-thread pattern). sticky can force-or-override severity defaults. The source enum is designed so a future agent feature can report session progress and "needs your decision" events as a first-class channel without reshaping this system (agent events are model-only in this change; no agent feature ships here).
Goals.R-6: Session notification history: every shown notification is appended to an in-memory session log (cap 50, FIFO, never persisted across launches). A command-palette entry ("Notifications: show recent" final label per locale) opens the history surface listing time, source, severity and full untruncated text (long messages that clamp on cards are complete here), each entry with a copy affordance. The palette is the only entry point in this change; a title-bar bell is a future candidate (owner, 2026-10-23: palette first).
Goals.R-7: Update notice migration: components/updateNotice renders through the shared card (info severity, its three existing buttons as actions[] entries — Update primary, Later normal, Skip version quiet) with zero change to store/autoUpdates semantics (INSTALL_UPDATE / DISMISS_NOTICE / SKIP_VERSION), skip persistence or once-per-launch gating. The C-66 archive contract remains the semantic owner; only the rendering moves.
Goals.R-8: Per-file banner stays a banner: components/editorWithTabs/notifications.vue keeps its queue semantics, per-tab attachment and confirm-with-safe-default behavior (file-changed-on-disk stays exactly there), but is reskinned to the shared tokens/typography/radius and its message text becomes selectable (user-select: none is removed; copy-on-select per R-3 applies).
Goals.R-9: Dead code removal: the SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING action in store/notification.js, its unit-test block in tests/renderer/store/notification.test.ts, and the orphan installPandoc locale key (all ten locales) are deleted. The "missing external tool" pattern for any future need is a warning card with an "Open website" action (as mocked); it is recorded in design-context, not implemented, because no live path reaches it today.
Goals.R-10: Localization: every new user-facing string — palette/history labels, source names, "More N notifications" plurals, built-in action labels (Copy / Retry / Open / Reveal) — lands as native copy in all ten static/locales/*.json, written per the Language Policy (not mechanically translated).

Constraints.Item: Theme tokens only: card chrome uses the float/editor/button token families plus the new severity tokens; every theme in src/renderer/src/assets/themes/ supplies the severity tokens (Paper/Ink values normative from the mock; other themes tuned to their palettes in the same change).

Call-site compatibility: the ~70 existing notice.notify / SHOW_NOTIFICATION call sites keep working; the service API change is additive (new optional fields) plus the showConfirm removal with its two migrated call sites. No caller is left un-migrated.

Boundary is normative: toasts inform and offer shortcuts; the banner asks contextual questions with a safe default; modals own decisions with no safe default or data risk. The silence test ("if the user never answers, is a safe state reached?") decides the surface, and no toast may require an answer.
The zoom indicator (C-49) keeps its own module, position, timing and contract; at most its styling aligns with shared tokens. It does not join the stack and its behavior is not touched.
Modal dialogs (unsavedCloseDialog and friends) are untouched; no dialog flow moves into a toast.
History is session-memory only; no persistence, no IPC, no disk writes.
Clipboard writes go through the existing renderer clipboard path with navigator.clipboard fallback as available in the WKWebView; failures never break card dismissal.
Accessibility: cards carry role="status" and aria-live="polite" (errors may use assertive); buttons keep focus-visible outlines (as mocked); Esc handling does not steal focus from the editor.
All governed edits ship MODULE_CONTRACT / MODULE_MAP / CHANGE_SUMMARY updates; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; graph and verification deltas land in the same bundle as the code.
English repo artifacts; the interactive 2026-10-23 mock stays out of the repo (design provenance lives in design-context.xml).

NonGoals.NonGoal: A title-bar bell or notification-center panel (palette entry only; bell is a future candidate once history proves useful).
Cross-session or on-disk notification history; OS-level native notifications.
The agent feature itself — only the agent source channel and event shapes are reserved; no agent events fire in this change.
Redesigning modal dialogs, the unsaved-close flow, or any file open/save dialog.
Changing the banner's queue/exclusiveType semantics beyond reskin and text selection.
Touching the zoom indicator beyond optional token alignment.
Per-source mute or Do Not Disturb modes (future, following the VS Code notification-center pattern).
Implementing the "missing external tool" warning card (no live caller; pattern recorded in design-context).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Visual gate: Playwright probe screenshots of one card per severity in Paper and Ink match the approved icon-chip design — chip tint at 14% severity color, chromeIcons geometry, C-66 metrics (radius, padding, shadow ring) — verified by crop + literal pixel probes on chip, stripe-free edge, timer hairline and button colors; no .mt-notification, notice-bg or fluent element is produced anywhere in the app (regression-pinned in tests).

Stack behavior (e2e): max 3 cards visible with an "More N notifications" chip (correct plurals in at least ru and en), hover pauses the timer hairline, Esc closes the topmost card, error cards never auto-dismiss, and a drag-selection inside a card does not dismiss it while an empty-selection click does.

Copy-on-select (e2e + unit): mouseup with a selection inside a card writes exactly the selected string to the clipboard; the double green pulse runs on the selection (both pulses pixel-captured in the probe) and the class is removed afterwards leaving the resting selection tint; under prefers-reduced-motion the copy still happens with no animation.

Actions contract: unit tests pin that actions[] rendering produces the three styles, built-in kinds dispatch their payload handlers, and no notify() return value resolves or rejects on button clicks; the migrated call sites (image-deletion copy, reveal-in-folder) behave as one-click shortcuts with no dangling Promise; showConfirm no longer exists in the service API.

Event model: unit tests pin severity x source defaults (error sticky, others timed), dedupKey collapsing (repeat under the same key bumps a visible counter instead of stacking), and the history log (cap 50 FIFO, full text retained, source recorded).

History surface: the palette lists the new command; opening it shows session notifications with time/source/severity and a per-entry copy action; the log survives card dismissal and never survives relaunch.

Update notice: e2e pins that Update / Later / Skip render through the shared card in the three button styles and dispatch the unchanged store actions (INSTALL_UPDATE / DISMISS_NOTICE / SKIP_VERSION); once-per-launch and skip persistence behave as before C-66 semantics.
Banner: reskinned to shared tokens; message text is selectable and copy-on-select works there too; queue semantics and file-changed-on-disk flow unchanged (existing specs stay green).
Dead code: SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING absent from the store, its test block removed, installPandoc key absent from all ten locales; no test or code references remain (grep-pinned).
Localization: all new strings present as native copy in all ten static/locales/*.json with verified placeholders and plurals.

npm test green; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; .grace/graph (runtime.xml notification flow entries, features.xml card-system module) and .grace/verification (card system, copy-on-select, history, actions entries) updated in the same change.

AffectedAreas.Item: src/renderer/src/services/notification/ (renderer rewrite: card markup, stack, timers, dedup, actions, copy-on-select; index.html/.css legacy Fluent files removed; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP updates)
src/renderer/src/store/notification.js (API passthrough with optional fields; SHOW_PANDOC_MISSING removal)
src/renderer/src/store/editor.js (two showConfirm call sites migrate to actions[])
src/renderer/src/components/updateNotice/index.vue (renders via shared card; store wiring unchanged)
src/renderer/src/components/commandPalette + commands registry (history command entry); new session-history store module
static/locales/*.json (ten locales: palette/history labels, source names, overflow plurals, action labels)
tests/renderer/services/notification*.test.js, tests/renderer/store/notification.test.ts (rewrite/removal), new card-system unit tests, visual probe spec, history/dedup/action tests
.grace/graph/runtime.xml + features.xml, .grace/verification/ routed documents (deltas in the same bundle)

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Pixel-probed Paper/Ink screenshots of all four severities (chip tint, no stripe, hairline, buttons); stack overflow chip with plural forms; Esc/hover/sticky behavior traces; copy-on-select clipboard equality plus both pulse frames captured; actions-contract units (no promise semantics, three styles, built-in kinds); dedupKey counter and history cap/FIFO units; update-notice e2e on unchanged store actions; dead-code grep pins; ten-locale key completeness; updated graph and verification documents with grace lint 0.

Assumptions.Assumption: The icon-chip variant is the owner's final visual pick (2026-10-23: "icon-chip is cleaner, we take it"); the stripe variant shown in the same mock session is rejected and stays only in the design record.

The double-pulse copy confirmation is final: the corner "Copied" pill and the selection-anchored "Copied" bubble were both rejected by the owner on 2026-10-23 as ugly / over-labeled; the pulse parameters (~1.1 s, two pulses, success-tinted) follow the approved mock behavior.

navigator.clipboard or the existing renderer clipboard shim is writable from the notification context in the WKWebView; if both are blocked the copy silently no-ops (feature degrades quietly, never errors at the user).
The palette history command can reuse the existing commandCenter registration path (view.command-palette pattern) without new shortcut machinery; no new global shortcut is introduced.

Severity token names and exact chip metrics may be refined by the plan within the approved mock's look (tint percentage, 26px chip, 15px glyph) without re-approval, as long as probe evidence matches the mock family.
